findings.title: Apiiro: Claude Code's “Don't Ask Again” Saves Approved Commands - Passwords Included - to settings.local.json; 2,539 Secrets Found on Public GitHub
findings.summary_md: Apiiro researchers Shmulik Cohen and Matan Giladi reported on 5 November 2026 that Claude Code saves an entire approved shell command, including any password or API key typed into it, verbatim into the project file .claude/settings.local.json when the user chooses Yes and don't ask again. Their scan of public GitHub found 104,185 copies of the file across 103,617 repositories, with 1,122 files holding at least one secret. Counting git history, shared settings, and saved agent transcripts, the exposure totaled 2,539 secrets across 1,994 repositories.

findings.title: Claude Code approval files found exposing company secrets on GitHub, says Apirro researchers
findings.summary_md: Research published on 5 November by Apiiro's Shmulik Cohen and Matan Giladi showed that Claude Code can retain a complete approved shell command, including credentials, in .claude/settings.local.json. The firm found 1,122 public copies of the file holding at least one secret, and broader scans surfaced 2,539 secrets across 1,994 public repositories. The exposure comes from the permanent approval option saving credential-bearing commands in plain text.

findings.title: Claude Code “Don't ask again” left secrets in 1,122 GitHub files
findings.summary_md: Apiiro's research, published 5 November, found that 1,122 of the 104,185 public copies of Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json on GitHub hold a real secret. Choosing Yes and don't ask again when Claude Code proposes a shell command writes the full command string, secret included, into the project settings file. That file is then easy to commit to a public repository, exposing passwords and keys.

findings.title: Apiiro’s Claude Code Scan Found 2,539 Secrets in .claude/settings.local.json - Local Desktop Tools Keep Credentials Off the Git Path
findings.summary_md: On 5 November 2026 Apiiro published a scan of public GitHub for Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json files, examining 104,185 copies across 103,617 repositories. It found 1,122 files containing at least one secret, totaling 1,379 distinct values in the current copies, with 2,539 secrets when history and transcripts are included. The post notes that local desktop tools avoid this class of leak entirely.
